title: Characterization of synaptic structural plasticity in mouse spinal dorsal horn neurons
protocol: Prepare the glass micropipette using a P-1000 micropipette puller set to heat 850, velocity 30, and time 250.
Trim about 1–2 mm of excess glass from the pulled capillary with microscissors.
Bevel the micropipette tip with a microforge to refine its length to about 4.5–5 mm.
Assemble the microinjection system comprising a stereotaxic instrument, microsyringe, micropump, spine clamps, and illumination lights.
Set up the stereotaxic frame.
Mount the microsyringe injector into the manipulator of the micropump.
Connect the injector to the controller.
Fix the microsyringe so that the vernier scale is visible.
Attach a glass micropipette to the microsyringe using Joint Teflon tubing.
Carefully fill the microsyringe and micropipette with mineral oil, ensuring no air bubbles remain in the micropipette.
Use aseptic techniques when handling the micropipette, avoiding contact with the tip.
Prepare the virus solution.
Defrost a stock aliquot of the required purified virus on ice.
Keep the defrosted virus on ice before injection.
If necessary, store the defrosted virus at 4°C for up to 3 days.
Dilute the virus particles with sterile 1x phosphate-buffered saline (1x PBS) if needed and prepare the appropriate amount of virus solution as required by the experiment.
Load the tip of the micropipette carefully into the virus solution.
Control the micropump connected to the micro syringe to load the virus solution at a rate of 200 nL/s.
Anesthetize animals before surgical site preparation for virus injection.
Weigh the animal using a digital scale.
Record the preoperative weight for determining anesthetic dose and postoperative monitoring.
Anesthetize mice with 5% isoflurane in an anesthesia induction chamber.
Place the mouse in the stereotaxic frame on a heat mat once asleep.
Maintain anesthesia at 2%-3% isoflurane throughout surgery.
Shave fur from the lower back to neck carefully.
Disinfect the shaved skin with 75% ethanol pads.
Repeat disinfection with 1% povidone-iodine three times.
Isolate the aseptically prepared site with a surgical drape.
Place lubricant eye ointment on each eye to prevent drying during surgery.
Reapply lubricant as necessary.
Incise the skin at the Th12-L3 level.
Fix the mouse on a stereoscope frame with lug rods.
Keep the mouse under 2%–3% isoflurane anesthesia.
Gently press fingers on the rib to find the Th12-L3 vertebra through the skin.
Use a No. 10 scalpel to make a 3–4 cm incision in the skin at the Th12-L3, exposing the muscle.
Gently stretch the skin and press firmly with the scalpel blade to ensure the incision is clean.
Stabilize the target vertebra.
Place the animal on a rolled-up tissue pad.
Lift the mouse onto the spine clamp of the stereoscopic frame.
Secure the animal to a stereotaxic frame using spinal clamps at the rostral and caudal sites of the incision.
Fixate the target vertebra to prevent movement due to breathing.
Locate the interspace between the Th13 and L1 vertebrae.
Separate the fascia covering the spine.
Remove the paraspinal muscle around the left side of the interspace between the Th13 and L1 vertebrae.
Use the 13th rib to locate the 13th thoracic vertebrate.
Locate L1 caudally in the vertebra that supports the 13th ribs.
Incise the dura mater and arachnoid membrane with a 30G needle to create a small hole.
Insert the glass micropipette approximately 500 μm lateral from the midline of the spinal dorsal horn.
Move the tip into the spinal dorsal horn at a depth of 250 μm from the surface of the dorsal root entry zone.
Keep exposed tissues moist with sterile 0.9% NaCl throughout surgery.
Wait for 2 minutes after positioning the glass micropipette to allow nervous tissue accommodation.
Set the injection volume of the pump as 500 nL.
Program the injection speed at 100 nL/min.
Press the start button on the pump to initiate the virus injection.
Check the scale after injection to see if the virus level decreases.
Leave the micropipette for 5 minutes to balance pressure.
Slowly withdraw the syringe.
Suture superficial tissue layers with absorbable 6-0 sutures.
Close skin with 6-0 non-absorbable nylon sutures.
Keep animal on a heating pad until recovery.
Anesthetize animals by injecting pentobarbital sodium (50 mg/kg, i.p.).
Perfuse transcardially with approximately 20 mL of 1x PBS.
Fix with ice-cold 4% paraformaldehyde/1x PBS.
Remove the whole spine.
Postfix with ice-cold 4% paraformaldehyde/1x PBS for about 12 hours at 4°C.
Place spinal cord in 30% sucrose solution for 24 hours at 4°C.
Dissect L3-L5 segments of the spinal cord.
Embed spinal cord section in OCT compound.
Section spinal cord into 40 μm thick transverse slices from anterior to posterior with cryostat.
Mount spinal cord sections on adhesive slide with cover glass using aqueous mounting medium containing DAPI.
Seal mounted solution with nail polish.
Capture wide dynamic range (WDR) neurons using a confocal microscope with a 63x oil immersion objective.
Take Z-series images at intervals of 0.37 mm for each dendrite.

Identify WDR neurons based on five criteria: located within laminae 4 and 5, EGFP-positive with complete dendritic impregnation, at least one dendrite extending into an adjacent lamina, primary dendrites remaining intact within tissue thickness, cell body diameter between 20 and 50 mm.
Measure the dendritic spines of EGFP-expressing neurons using 3D confocal stacks in Imaris software.
Classify dendritic spines based on a clear head structure.
Count the dendritic spines from the secondary and tertiary segments of the dendrite using the Imaris filament tool.
Record the length of selected dendrites and the number of dendritic spines.
Determine the dendrite spine density by calculating the number of spines per dendrite length.
Express the spine density as the number of spines per 10 μm of dendrites.
Isolate the spinal dorsal horn from the 4th lumbar of mice.
Homogenize the tissue in cold lysis buffer 1.
Centrifuge the homogenized sample at 15,000 g for 30 min at 4°C.
Measure the soluble actin (G-actin) in the supernatant.
Resuspend the insoluble F-actin pellet in lysis buffer plus an equal volume of buffer 2.
Incubate the resuspended sample on ice for 1 hour with gentle mixing every 15 minutes to convert F-actin into soluble G-actin.
Centrifuge the samples at 15,000 g for 30 min at 4°C.
Measure the F-actin in this supernatant.
Proportionally load the samples from the supernatant (G-actin) and pellet (F-actin) fractions.
Analyze the loaded samples by western blotting.
